sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol and Drug Impact on the Driving Ability

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Every drug can dull driving, from store-bought and prescribed medicines through illegal drugs and alcohol, striking the mental and physical skills behind emergency reactions, varying by body weight, mood, dose, and timing, while safe driving always wants observant eyes, steady hands, and clear heads [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Drink and drugs first steal judgment and sight, slowing sound reactions and wrecking speed estimates until reason vanishes, mixed drugs stack dangers with alcohol masking companions, so doctors or pharmacists preview every combination especially tranquilizers and sedatives [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
Marijuana's social doses cloud concentration, judgment, and driving senses, heavy amphetamines trade sleeplessness for clumsiness and crash risk, cocaine lapses attention, caffeine never sobers drunks, tranquilizers and barbiturate sleep aids depress heavily, store medicines like antihistamines and cold cures drowse, every drug earns suspicion, and alcohol itself depresses coordination, judgment, perception, and mood while boosting tranquilizers [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Twenty eighteen Texas counted nine hundred forty dead with alcohol-impaired drivers at twenty-six percent of traffic deaths, federal counts tag teen crashes as top teen killers with three thousand two hundred fifty-five teen drivers in twenty seventeen fatal crashes at nearly twenty-five percent drinking and nearly seven percent of twenty eighteen fatal crashes tied to under-twenty-one drinkers, minors hold zero allowed blood alcohol, adults intoxicate at point zero eight or more, and DWI and DUI arrests humiliate while fining up to ten thousand dollars before lawyers and courts [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A02
Open alcohol containers stay illegal in highway vehicle passenger areas moving, stopped, or parked, fining up to five hundred dollars, while cold showers, black coffee, and exercise never sober anyone since only time across weight, drinks, and food clears about one drink hourly, so sober companions drive [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A02
Minors under twenty-one never buy, attempt, drink, or hold alcohol, and zero tolerance criminalizes any detectable alcohol while operating vehicles or watercraft publicly as minor DUI, with parallel non-driving bans on buying, attempting, false twenty-one claims, fake age papers, drinking, and holding, while suppliers risk four thousand dollars and a year in jail [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A02
Minor non-driving penalties open Class C up to five hundred dollars with eight to twelve service hours, a mandatory course with possible parent attendance under eighteen, and thirty suspended days, repeat Class C up to five hundred dollars with twenty to forty hours, a possible course, and sixty days, triple under seventeen Class C up to five hundred dollars with twenty to forty hours, a possible course, and sixty days or juvenile court, and triple at seventeen to twenty-one Class B of two hundred fifty to two thousand dollars with forty to sixty hours, a possible course, up to one hundred eighty jailed days, and one hundred eighty suspended days without deferred outcomes from the third conviction on, plus invalid-license penalties for moving violations during suspension [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A02
Arrested intoxicated or detectably alcohol-touched minors publicly operating vehicles or watercraft imply consent to breath or blood testing that reports alcohol presence, alcohol amount, and other drugs, with refusals suspending licenses or privileges [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A03
Minor specimen refusals suspend one hundred eighty days first and two years after, detectable-but-below-point-zero-eight failures suspend sixty, one hundred twenty, then one hundred eighty days, and hearings can contest suspensions [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A03
Minor DUI opens Class C up to five hundred dollars with twenty to forty hours and a mandatory course with possible parent attendance under eighteen, repeats Class C up to five hundred dollars with forty to sixty hours and a possible course, triples under seventeen Class C up to five hundred dollars with forty to sixty hours and a possible course or juvenile transfer, and triples at seventeen to twenty-one Class B of five hundred to two thousand dollars and up to one hundred eighty jailed days with forty to sixty hours, a possible course, and one year suspended or ninety days with a judge-ordered ignition interlock, without deferred outcomes on the third offense [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A03
Minor DWI opens Class B up to two thousand dollars with seventy-two hours to one hundred eighty jailed days and three hundred sixty-five suspended days or ninety with interlock, probation and waiver only first time with open containers forcing six-day minimums, repeats Class A up to four thousand dollars with thirty days to a year jailed and one hundred eighty days to eighteen months suspended, triples into third-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten TDCJ years and one hundred eighty days to eighteen months suspended, child passengers under fifteen draw state jail felony up to ten thousand dollars with one hundred eighty days to two years caged and ninety days to a year suspended, intoxication assault draws third-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten years and ninety days to a year suspended, and intoxication manslaughter draws second-degree felony up to ten thousand dollars with two to twenty years and one hundred eighty days to two years suspended [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A04
Adult implied consent mirrors minors including detectably touched drivers up to twenty-one, refusals suspending one hundred eighty days first and up to seven hundred thirty after, point-zero-eight-or-greater failures suspending ninety days first and up to three hundred sixty-five after, with point zero eight or more always intoxicated [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A04
Adult DWI and DUI open up to two thousand dollars with seventy-two hours to one hundred eighty jailed days and ninety to three hundred sixty-five suspended days, repeat up to four thousand dollars with thirty days to a year jailed and one hundred eighty days to two years suspended, triple up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten TDCJ years and one hundred eighty days to two years suspended, child passengers under fifteen draw up to ten thousand dollars with one hundred eighty days to two state-jailed years and ninety days to two years suspended, intoxication assault draws up to ten thousand dollars with two to ten years and ninety days to two years suspended, and intoxication manslaughter draws up to ten thousand dollars with two to twenty years and one hundred eighty days to two years suspended [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0064]
